input.new_string:
Steps 1–4 are worth doing on their own: they are a refactor of working code with
tests already in place, and they are what makes step 5 tractable.

### 3.7 A command-mode key that works from inside a text field

Requested: enter command mode with a modifier chord rather than a bare `:`,
because the application is full of text inputs and inside one a `:` does nothing
but insert a colon.

The complaint is accurate and the current design concedes it. `internal/app/app.go:466`
routes `:` through `maybeEnterInCommandMode`, which asks the view whether it is
in edit mode (`FormView.InEditMode()`) and, if it is, forwards the keystroke to
the active input instead. So command mode is unreachable from any form, filter
box or search field — which is most of the application.

An escape hatch already exists and shows the shape of the problem: the
`CommandModeView` interface (`app.go:44`) lets a view declare that `:` should
enter command mode even while `InEditMode()` is true. Exactly one view
implements it — `internal/ui/netdiag/update.go:18` — and only for the topology
tab in its ready state, where nothing is being edited anyway. It papers over a
routing quirk; it does not give the user a way in while typing.

#### `ctrl+:` specifically cannot be made to work

Worth settling before any code is written. A terminal encodes Ctrl by clearing
bits, which only covers ASCII `@` through `_` (0x40–0x5F) plus a handful of
aliases. `:` is 0x3A and has no control encoding: pressing Ctrl+: sends either a
plain `:` or nothing at all. Reporting it as a distinct key needs the Kitty
keyboard protocol or xterm's `modifyOtherKeys`, and bubbletea v1.3.10 implements
neither — the module has no reference to either. A `case "ctrl+:"` would be dead
code.

#### What does work

| Option | Portability | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `alt+:` | Good | bubbletea v1 reports `alt+<rune>` from the ESC-prefix convention; works wherever "Alt sends Escape" is on, which is the default nearly everywhere. Closest to the request. |
| A free `ctrl+<letter>` | Total | The bindings in use are `ctrl+a c d e f k n o r s w y`; `ctrl+i m j h [` are aliases of Tab, Enter, LF, Backspace and Esc and must be left alone. That leaves `b g l p t u v x z` — `ctrl+p` and `ctrl+g` read best. |
| `esc` then `:` | Total | Vim-like, but `esc` already means cancel / go back everywhere (Rule 111), so it would need a mode timer. Not recommended. |

**Recommendation: keep `:` and add one chord that always wins**, rather than
replacing `:`. Muscle memory survives, and the new binding needs no
`InEditMode()` check at all — `handleKeyMsg` sees every `tea.KeyMsg` before any
view does, so a `case` there takes priority unconditionally. That is the whole
implementation: three lines next to the existing `case ":"`.

#### Ripple

- `internal/app/app_header.go:56` renders `:` as the inactive command prompt —
  it should show whichever key is authoritative.
- `internal/app/app_test.go:30` asserts the `:` shortcut.
- Rules 114, 130 and 137: every view's `GetShortcuts()` / `GetHelpContent()` that
  mentions `:`. Three views were already caught drifting on this kind of change
  (§1.1), so the check that each advertised key appears in the help — now present
  in `status`, `containers` and `workspaces` — is the thing to lean on.
- `CommandModeView` / `AllowCommandMode` become deletable if the new chord always
  wins, since the sole reason they exist disappears. One implementation to
  remove.

---

## 4. Existing plans

J'ai mergé #15 d'abord, puis ajouté l'entrée en §3.7 du backlog : https://github.com/anthnel/devdesk/pull/16

**Ta remarque est exacte, et le code la concède déjà.** `app.go:466` fait passer `:` par `maybeEnterInCommandMode`, qui redirige la touche vers l'input actif dès que `FormView.InEditMode()` est vrai. Il existe même une échappatoire dédiée — l'interface `CommandModeView` — mais sa seule implémentation (`netdiag/update.go:18`) ne se déclenche que sur l'onglet topology en état ready, c'est-à-dire là où justement rien n'est en édition. Elle contourne un problème de routage, elle ne t'ouvre pas la porte pendant que tu tapes.

**En revanche `ctrl+:` précisément ne peut pas marcher**, et ça valait la peine de le trancher avant d'écrire une ligne. Un terminal encode Ctrl en effaçant des bits, ce qui ne couvre que l'ASCII `@`–`_` (0x40–0x5F). `:` vaut 0x3A : Ctrl+: envoie soit un `:` nu, soit rien. Le remonter comme touche distincte demande le protocole clavier Kitty ou `modifyOtherKeys` de xterm, et bubbletea v1.3.10 n'implémente ni l'un ni l'autre (aucune référence dans le module). Un `case "ctrl+:"` serait du code mort.

Ce qui marche, avec l'inventaire des bindings déjà pris :

| Option | Portabilité | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `alt+:` | bonne | bubbletea v1 remonte `alt+<rune>` via la convention préfixe ESC ; marche partout où « Alt sends Escape » est actif, le défaut quasi partout. Le plus proche de ta demande. |
| `ctrl+<lettre>` libre | totale | Pris : `a c d e f k n o r s w y`. `ctrl+i m j h [` sont Tab/Entrée/LF/Backspace/Esc, à ne pas toucher. Restent `b g l p t u v x z` — `ctrl+p` ou `ctrl+g` se lisent bien. |
| `esc` puis `:` | totale | Façon vim, mais `esc` veut déjà dire annuler/retour partout (Rule 111). Pas recommandé. |

Ma recommandation, notée comme telle dans l'entrée : **garder `:` et ajouter un chord qui gagne toujours**, plutôt que remplacer. La mémoire musculaire survit, et le nouveau binding n'a besoin d'aucune vérification `InEditMode()` — `handleKeyMsg` voit tous les `tea.KeyMsg` avant n'importe quelle vue, donc un `case` à cet endroit passe devant inconditionnellement. Trois lignes à côté du `case ":"` existant.

Le ripple est cartographié : le prompt du header (`app_header.go:56`), `app_test.go:30`, l'aide de chaque vue (Rules 114/130/137 — et trois vues ont déjà dérivé sur ce genre de changement), et `CommandModeView` qui devient supprimable une fois le nouveau binding en place.

Il te reste à choisir la touche — c'est la seule décision qui bloque l'implémentation.

An escape hatch already exists and shows the shape of the problem: the
`CommandModeView` interface (`app.go:44`) lets a view declare that `:` should
enter command mode even while `InEditMode()` is true. Exactly one view
implements it — `internal/ui/netdiag/update.go:18` — and only for the topology
tab in its ready state, where nothing is being edited anyway. It papers over a
routing quirk; it does not give the user a way in while typing.

#### Worked example: the security view

`internal/ui/security/model.go:296` returns `InEditMode() == true` for focused
fields 1, 7 and 10 — target path, Trivy server, Gitleaks config. Field 7 is the
case that makes the point: its own placeholder is `https://trivy-server:4954`,
so the field has to accept **two** colons to hold a valid value. Forwarding `:`
to the input there is not a bug to fix; it is the only correct behaviour.

Which is exactly why `:` is the wrong key for command mode. The user's only
route out today is to move focus to a field that happens not to take text — a
checkbox — and press `:` there. Command-mode reachability ends up depending on
which control is focused, and nothing tells the user that.

`InEditMode()` is broader still: it is also true for `StateScanning`,
`StateResults` and `StateDetails`, and `m.confirmModal != nil`. In those states
there is no field to move focus to, so `:` is forwarded to the view, which has
no `case` for it and drops it silently — no view in the application handles `:`
itself. Reaching command mode from a results table means pressing `esc` to
leave the results first. That is the same defect as the text field, without

Exactement, et c'est le meilleur exemple possible — je l'ai ajouté à l'entrée (#16 mis à jour).

`internal/ui/security/model.go:296` renvoie `InEditMode() == true` pour les champs 1, 7 et 10 — target path, Trivy server, Gitleaks config. Le champ 7 est parlant parce que son propre placeholder est `https://trivy-server:4954` : il doit accepter **deux** `:` pour contenir une valeur valide. Rediriger `:` vers l'input là n'est pas un bug à corriger, c'est le seul comportement correct.

C'est précisément ce qui disqualifie `:` comme touche de mode commande. Ta seule sortie aujourd'hui, c'est de déplacer le focus sur un champ qui ne prend pas de texte — une checkbox — et de presser `:` là. La joignabilité du mode commande dépend donc du contrôle qui a le focus, et rien ne le signale à l'utilisateur.

Et c'est pire que ce que tu décris. `InEditMode()` est aussi vrai pour `StateScanning`, `StateResults`, `StateDetails` et quand une confirm modal est ouverte. Dans ces états **il n'y a aucun champ vers lequel déplacer le focus** : le `:` est transmis à la vue, qui n'a pas de `case` pour lui et le jette silencieusement — j'ai vérifié, aucune vue de l'application ne traite `:` elle-même. Depuis un tableau de résultats de scan, atteindre le mode commande impose de faire `esc` pour quitter les résultats d'abord. Même défaut, sans même le contournement.

Ça renforce la recommandation : le nouveau chord doit être intercepté dans `handleKeyMsg` **avant** le fork `InEditMode()`, sans condition. C'est ce qui le rend joignable depuis le champ Trivy server *et* depuis la table de résultats, alors que `CommandModeView` — qui essaie de résoudre ça vue par vue — ne peut couvrir ni l'un ni l'autre.
qu'est ce que tu entends par nouveau chord

Du jargon de ma part, désolé — « chord » c'est simplement **une combinaison de touches pressées ensemble**, du type `ctrl+p` ou `alt+:`, par opposition à une touche seule comme `:`. Le terme vient du clavier de piano (plusieurs touches à la fois) et s'oppose à une *séquence* comme `esc` puis `:`, où on presse l'une après l'autre.

Donc « le nouveau chord » = la nouvelle combinaison qu'on choisira pour entrer en mode commande, quelle qu'elle soit : `alt+:`, `ctrl+p`, `ctrl+g`…

Le terme apparaît deux fois dans l'entrée du backlog (§3.7). Je peux le remplacer par « modifier combination », plus lisible, si tu préfères — dis-moi.

Et la décision qui reste bloquante, c'est laquelle de ces combinaisons tu veux :

| Candidat | Argument |
|---|---|
| `alt+:` | le plus proche de ta demande d'origine, garde le `:` dans le geste |
| `ctrl+p` | portabilité totale, aucun terminal exotique requis |
| `ctrl+g` | idem, et `g` est libre partout dans l'app |

536	
537	### 3.7 A command-mode key that works from inside a text field
538	
539	Requested: enter command mode with a modifier chord rather than a bare `:`,
540	because the application is full of text inputs and inside one a `:` does nothing
541	but insert a colon.
542	
543	The complaint is accurate and the current design concedes it. `internal/app/app.go:466`
544	routes `:` through `maybeEnterInCommandMode`, which asks the view whether it is
545	in edit mode (`FormView.InEditMode()`) and, if it is, forwards the keystroke to
546	the active input instead. So command mode is unreachable from any form, filter
547	box or search field — which is most of the application.
548	
549	An escape hatch already exists and shows the shape of the problem: the
550	`CommandModeView` interface (`app.go:44`) lets a view declare that `:` should
551	enter command mode even while `InEditMode()` is true. Exactly one view
552	implements it — `internal/ui/netdiag/update.go:18` — and only for the topology
553	tab in its ready state, where nothing is being edited anyway. It papers over a
554	routing quirk; it does not give the user a way in while typing.
555	
556	#### Worked example: the security view
557	
558	`internal/ui/security/model.go:296` returns `InEditMode() == true` for focused
559	fields 1, 7 and 10 — target path, Trivy server, Gitleaks config. Field 7 is the
560	case that makes the point: its own placeholder is `https://trivy-server:4954`,
561	so the field has to accept **two** colons to hold a valid value. Forwarding `:`
562	to the input there is not a bug to fix; it is the only correct behaviour.
563	
564	Which is exactly why `:` is the wrong key for command mode. The user's only
565	route out today is to move focus to a field that happens not to take text — a
566	checkbox — and press `:` there. Command-mode reachability ends up depending on
567	which control is focused, and nothing tells the user that.
568	
569	`InEditMode()` is broader still: it is also true for `StateScanning`,
570	`StateResults` and `StateDetails`, and `m.confirmModal != nil`. In those states
571	there is no field to move focus to, so `:` is forwarded to the view, which has
572	no `case` for it and drops it silently — no view in the application handles `:`
573	itself. Reaching command mode from a results table means pressing `esc` to
574	leave the results first. That is the same defect as the text field, without
575	even a workaround.
576	
577	#### `ctrl+:` specifically cannot be made to work
578	
579	Worth settling before any code is written. A terminal encodes Ctrl by clearing
580	bits, which only covers ASCII `@` through `_` (0x40–0x5F) plus a handful of
581	aliases. `:` is 0x3A and has no control encoding: pressing Ctrl+: sends either a
582	plain `:` or nothing at all. Reporting it as a distinct key needs the Kitty
583	keyboard protocol or xterm's `modifyOtherKeys`, and bubbletea v1.3.10 implements
584	neither — the module has no reference to either. A `case "ctrl+:"` would be dead
585	code.
586	
587	#### What does work
588	
589	| Option | Portability | Notes |
590	|---|---|---|
591	| `alt+:` | Good | bubbletea v1 reports `alt+<rune>` from the ESC-prefix convention; works wherever "Alt sends Escape" is on, which is the default nearly everywhere. Closest to the request. |
592	| A free `ctrl+<letter>` | Total | The bindings in use are `ctrl+a c d e f k n o r s w y`; `ctrl+i m j h [` are aliases of Tab, Enter, LF, Backspace and Esc and must be left alone. That leaves `b g l p t u v x z` — `ctrl+p` and `ctrl+g` read best. |
593	| `esc` then `:` | Total | Vim-like, but `esc` already means cancel / go back everywhere (Rule 111), so it would need a mode timer. Not recommended. |
594	
595	**Recommendation: keep `:` and add one chord that always wins**, rather than
596	replacing `:`. Muscle memory survives, and the new binding needs no
597	`InEditMode()` check at all — `handleKeyMsg` sees every `tea.KeyMsg` before any

### 3.7 A command-mode key that works from inside a text field

Requested: enter command mode with a modifier chord rather than a bare `:`,
because the application is full of text inputs and inside one a `:` does nothing
but insert a colon.

The complaint is accurate and the current design concedes it. `internal/app/app.go:466`
routes `:` through `maybeEnterInCommandMode`, which asks the view whether it is
in edit mode (`FormView.InEditMode()`) and, if it is, forwards the keystroke to
the active input instead. So command mode is unreachable from any form, filter
box or search field — which is most of the application.

An escape hatch already exists and shows the shape of the problem: the
`CommandModeView` interface (`app.go:44`) lets a view declare that `:` should
enter command mode even while `InEditMode()` is true. Exactly one view
implements it — `internal/ui/netdiag/update.go:18` — and only for the topology
tab in its ready state, where nothing is being edited anyway. It papers over a
routing quirk; it does not give the user a way in while typing.

#### Worked example: the security view

`internal/ui/security/model.go:296` returns `InEditMode() == true` for focused
fields 1, 7 and 10 — target path, Trivy server, Gitleaks config. Field 7 is the
case that makes the point: its own placeholder is `https://trivy-server:4954`,
so the field has to accept **two** colons to hold a valid value. Forwarding `:`
to the input there is not a bug to fix; it is the only correct behaviour.

Which is exactly why `:` is the wrong key for command mode. The user's only
route out today is to move focus to a field that happens not to take text — a
checkbox — and press `:` there. Command-mode reachability ends up depending on
which control is focused, and nothing tells the user that.

`InEditMode()` is broader still: it is also true for `StateScanning`,
`StateResults` and `StateDetails`, and `m.confirmModal != nil`. In those states
there is no field to move focus to, so `:` is forwarded to the view, which has
no `case` for it and drops it silently — no view in the application handles `:`
itself. Reaching command mode from a results table means pressing `esc` to
leave the results first. That is the same defect as the text field, without
even a workaround.

#### `ctrl+:` specifically cannot be made to work

Worth settling before any code is written. A terminal encodes Ctrl by clearing
bits, which only covers ASCII `@` through `_` (0x40–0x5F) plus a handful of
aliases. `:` is 0x3A and has no control encoding: pressing Ctrl+: sends either a
plain `:` or nothing at all. Reporting it as a distinct key needs the Kitty
keyboard protocol or xterm's `modifyOtherKeys`, and bubbletea v1.3.10 implements
neither — the module has no reference to either. A `case "ctrl+:"` would be dead
code.

#### What does work

| Option | Portability | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `alt+:` | Good | bubbletea v1 reports `alt+<rune>` from the ESC-prefix convention; works wherever "Alt sends Escape" is on, which is the default nearly everywhere. Closest to the request. |
| A free `ctrl+<letter>` | Total | The bindings in use are `ctrl+a c d e f k n o r s w y`; `ctrl+i m j h [` are aliases of Tab, Enter, LF, Backspace and Esc and must be left alone. That leaves `b g l p t u v x z` — `ctrl+p` and `ctrl+g` read best. |
| `esc` then `:` | Total | Vim-like, but `esc` already means cancel / go back everywhere (Rule 111), so it would need a mode timer. Not recommended. |

**Recommendation: keep `:` and add one chord that always wins**, rather than
replacing `:`. Muscle memory survives, and the new binding needs no
`InEditMode()` check at all — `handleKeyMsg` sees every `tea.KeyMsg` before any
view does, so a `case` there takes priority unconditionally. That is the whole
implementation: three lines next to the existing `case ":"`.

#### Ripple

- `internal/app/app_header.go:56` renders `:` as the inactive command prompt —
  it should show whichever key is authoritative.
- `internal/app/app_test.go:30` asserts the `:` shortcut.
- Rules 114, 130 and 137: every view's `GetShortcuts()` / `GetHelpContent()` that
  mentions `:`. Three views were already caught drifting on this kind of change
  (§1.1), so the check that each advertised key appears in the help — now present
  in `status`, `containers` and `workspaces` — is the thing to lean on.
- `CommandModeView` / `AllowCommandMode` become deletable if the new chord always
  wins, since the sole reason they exist disappears. One implementation to
  remove.

### 3.7 Command mode from inside a text field — **done**

`alt+:` now opens the command line from anywhere, including a focused text
input. A bare `:` keeps its old, conditional behaviour, so muscle memory
survives.

The problem: `handleKeyMsg` routed `:` through `maybeEnterInCommandMode`, which
asked the view whether it was in edit mode (`FormView.InEditMode()`) and, if it
was, forwarded the keystroke to the active input. Command mode was therefore
unreachable from any form, filter box or search field — most of the application.

The security view is the case that settles it. `InEditMode()` is true there for
the target path, Trivy server and Gitleaks config fields, and the Trivy server
placeholder is `https://trivy-server:4954` — the field has to accept **two**
colons to hold a valid value. Forwarding `:` to the input is not a bug; it is
the only correct behaviour, which is precisely why `:` cannot be the
authoritative key. The only way in was to move focus to a control that takes no
text and press `:` there, so reachability depended on which widget was focused
and nothing said so.

It was worse in `StateScanning`, `StateResults`, `StateDetails` and while a
confirm modal is open: `InEditMode()` is true and there is no field to move
focus to. `:` was forwarded to the view, which has no `case` for it — no view in
the application handles `:` itself — and dropped silently.

#### Why `alt+`, not `ctrl+`

`ctrl+:` cannot be made to work, and this is the note that should stop anyone
reintroducing it. A terminal encodes Ctrl by clearing bits, which only covers
ASCII `@` through `_` (0x40–0x5F). `:` is 0x3A: Ctrl+: sends a plain `:` or
nothing. Reporting it as a distinct key needs the Kitty keyboard protocol or
xterm's `modifyOtherKeys`, and bubbletea v1.3.10 implements neither. A
`case "ctrl+:"` would be dead code.

Alt has no such limit — a terminal sends ESC then the key, and bubbletea reports
that as the key carrying `Alt`. The alternative considered was a free
`ctrl+<letter>` (`b g l p t u v x z` are unused; `ctrl+i m j h [` are Tab, Enter,
LF, Backspace and Esc and must be left alone), which is marginally more portable
but loses the `:` in the gesture.

#### What shipped

- `altCommandModeKey` is handled in `handleKeyMsg` **before** the `InEditMode()`
  fork, so no view can claim it. The router sees every `tea.KeyMsg` first, which
  is what makes the binding unconditional.
- `enterCommandMode()` extracted; `maybeEnterInCommandMode` now only answers the
  bare `:`.
- `testutil.Key` understands an `alt+` prefix, building the key with the `Alt`
  modifier rather than the five literal runes `alt+:`. Both round-trip through
  `String()`, but only one is the message the application actually receives.
- Every `GetShortcuts()` and `GetHelpContent()` advertising `:` now advertises
  `alt+:` (Rules 114, 130, 137). The dashboard's Navigation help section carries
  the nuance in prose, so the other eight sites stay one line each.
- The header still renders `:` as the inactive prompt: it is the command line's
  visual marker, not a key legend, and `:` remains valid whenever no field has
  focus.

Two things the ripple list got wrong, corrected here: `app_test.go:30` is a
layout fixture for `buildShortcutLines`, not an assertion about the binding, so
it was left alone. And `CommandModeView` / `AllowCommandMode` was not merely
made redundant by this change — **it was already dead code**. The router only
consulted it when `InEditMode()` was true, and netdiag's implementation returns
true only on the topology tab, where `InEditMode()` is unconditionally false. It
could never fire. Deleted, along with its one implementation;
`TestCommandModeOnTheTopologyTab` became
`TestTheTopologyTabNeverBlocksCommandMode` and records why.

`alt+:` est implémenté — #16 est passé de « entrée backlog » à la feature complète, CI verte (lint 0 issue, tests + race detector).

**Le cœur du changement** tient en une ligne bien placée : `altCommandModeKey` est traité dans `handleKeyMsg` **avant** le fork `InEditMode()`. Le routeur voit tous les `tea.KeyMsg` avant n'importe quelle vue, donc aucun champ texte ne peut le réclamer. `:` garde son comportement conditionnel — la mémoire musculaire survit.

**Deux surprises en cours de route :**

`CommandModeView` / `AllowCommandMode` n'est pas devenu redondant avec ce changement — **c'était déjà du code mort**. Le routeur ne le consultait que quand `InEditMode()` était vrai, et l'unique implémentation (netdiag) ne couvre que l'onglet topology, où `InEditMode()` renvoie `false` inconditionnellement. Il ne pouvait jamais se déclencher. Supprimé ; `TestCommandModeOnTheTopologyTab` devient `TestTheTopologyTabNeverBlocksCommandMode` et documente pourquoi.

Et `app_test.go:30`, que j'avais listé dans le ripple comme « assertion sur le raccourci `:` », est en fait une fixture de layout pour `buildShortcutLines` — la liste de raccourcis y est arbitraire. Laissée telle quelle.

**Un détail de test qui compte :** `testutil.Key("alt+:")` construisait naïvement les cinq runes `a l t + :`, dont le `String()` vaut aussi `"alt+:"`. Le test serait passé sans rien prouver. `Key` comprend maintenant le préfixe `alt+` et pose le modificateur `Alt` sur la touche qui suit — c'est-à-dire exactement le message que bubbletea délivre quand le terminal envoie ESC puis `:`. `testutil` reste à 100 %.

Le header garde `:` comme prompt inactif : c'est le marqueur visuel de la ligne de commande, pas une légende de touche.

371		if len(columns) >= numColumns {
372			columns[0].Width = int(float64(available) * colTypeRatio)
373			columns[1].Width = int(float64(available) * colNameRatio)
374			columns[2].Width = int(float64(available) * colSlugRatio)
375			columns[3].Width = int(float64(available) * colVisibilityRatio)
376			columns[4].Width = int(float64(available) * colRoleRatio)
377			columns[5].Width = int(float64(available) * colCreatedRatio)
378			columns[6].Width = int(float64(available) * colActivityRatio)
379			// Last column gets the remainder
380			columns[7].Width = available - columns[0].Width - columns[1].Width - columns[2].Width - columns[3].Width - columns[4].Width - columns[5].Width - columns[6].Width
381			m.table.SetColumns(columns)
382		}
383	}

385	// updateTableRows rebuilds table rows from current items (sorted), applying active filters
386	func (m *Model) updateTableRows() {
387		query := strings.ToLower(m.filterBar.SearchQuery())
388		items := m.sortedItems(m.currentItems())
389		rows := make([]table.Row, 0, len(items))
390		for _, node := range items {
391			if query != "" {
392				nameMatch := strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(node.Name), query)
393				pathMatch := strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(node.FullPath), query)
394				if !nameMatch && !pathMatch {
395					continue
396				}
397			}
398			rows = append(rows, table.Row{
399				nodeTypeLabel(node),
400				node.Name,
401				nodeSlug(node.FullPath),
402				visibilityLabel(node),
403				node.AccessLevelName(),
404				timeAgo(node.CreatedAt),
405				timeAgo(node.LastActivityAt),
406				pipelineStatusLabel(node),
407			})
408		}
409		m.table.SetRows(rows)
410		m.updateSortIndicators()
411	}
412	
413	// cycleSort cycles through sort options: each column asc then desc, then next column
414	func (m Model) cycleSort() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
415		if m.sortAsc {
416			m.sortAsc = false
417		} else {
418			m.sortAsc = true
419			nextIdx := 0
420			for i, col := range sortableColumns {
421				if col == m.sortColumn {
422					nextIdx = (i + 1) % len(sortableColumns)
423					break
424				}
425			}
426			m.sortColumn = sortableColumns[nextIdx]
427		}
428		m.updateTableRows()
429		return m, nil
430	}
431	
432	// sortedItems returns nodes sorted by the current sort column and direction
433	func (m *Model) sortedItems(items []*TreeNode) []*TreeNode {
434		if len(items) == 0 {
435			return items
436		}
437	
438		sorted := make([]*TreeNode, len(items))
439		copy(sorted, items)
440	
441		sort.Slice(sorted, func(i, j int) bool {
442			a, b := sorted[i], sorted[j]
443	
444			var less bool
445			switch m.sortColumn {
446			case sortByName:
447				less = strings.ToLower(a.Name) < strings.ToLower(b.Name)
448			case sortByVisibility:
449				less = strings.ToLower(a.Visibility) < strings.ToLower(b.Visibility)
450			case sortByCreated:
451				less = timeBefore(a.CreatedAt, b.CreatedAt)
452			case sortByActivity:
453				less = timeBefore(a.LastActivityAt, b.LastActivityAt)
454			default: // sortByType
455				less = string(a.Type) < string(b.Type)
456			}
457	
458			if m.sortAsc {
459				return less
460			}
461			return !less
462		})
463	
464		return sorted
465	}
466	
467	// timeBefore compares two nullable times (nil is considered "oldest")
468	func timeBefore(a, b *time.Time) bool {
469		if a == nil && b == nil {
470			return false
471		}
472		if a == nil {
473			return true
474		}
475		if b == nil {
476			return false
477		}
478		return a.Before(*b)
479	}

481	// updateSortIndicators updates column headers with ▲/▼ sort arrows
482	func (m *Model) updateSortIndicators() {
483		sortColIndex := map[sortField]int{
484			sortByType:       0,
485			sortByName:       1,
486			sortByVisibility: 3,
487			sortByCreated:    5,
488			sortByActivity:   6,
489		}
490		baseTitles := map[int]string{
491			0: "Type",
492			1: "Name",
493			3: "Visibility",
494			5: "Created",
495			6: "Activity",
496		}
497	
498		columns := m.table.Columns()
499		if len(columns) < numColumns {
500			return
501		}
502	
503		// Reset sortable column titles
504		for idx, title := range baseTitles {
505			columns[idx].Title = title
506		}
507	
508		// Add arrow to active sort column
509		if idx, ok := sortColIndex[m.sortColumn]; ok {
510			arrow := " ▲"
511			if !m.sortAsc {
512				arrow = " ▼"
513			}
514			columns[idx].Title = baseTitles[idx] + arrow
515		}
516	
517		m.table.SetColumns(columns)
518	}

528			return m, nil
529		}

test: cover the gitlab explorer and fix three defects it exposed

Step 1 of three for this package: surface tests driving Update() and View()
only, so the split that follows is not written against a layout about to
change. 0% -> 58.1%.

Three defects the tests exposed, each pinned by a test that failed first:

- Actions resolved the cursor against the unfiltered list while the table
  showed the filtered one. With a filter active, ctrl+d, p, → and ctrl+w all
  acted on a different resource than the highlighted row — deleting the wrong
  group is the worst case. handleKeyMsg and GetShortcuts now go through
  visibleItems(), the same list updateTableRows builds from.

- bubbles does not clamp the table cursor when the row count shrinks, so
  narrowing the filter left it past the end: nothing highlighted and every
  action silently doing nothing. Same defect fixed in workspaces (#15); the
  drill-down path was already safe because it calls GotoTop().

- handleDeleteComplete set footerError with no clear timer, so a failed delete
  left the message on screen permanently (Rule 128).
EOF

Troisième paquet de la phase 3 fait : https://github.com/anthnel/devdesk/pull/17 — CI verte (lint 0 issue, tests + race detector).

| | Couverture | `model.go` |
|---|---|---|
| avant | 0 % | 1402 lignes |
| étape 1 (surface) | **58,1 %** | 1402 |
| étape 2 (découpe) | **58,1 %** | **206** |
| étape 3 (complément) | **91,5 %** | 206 |
| global | 43,6 % → **49,3 %** | |

Trois paquets, trois fois la même chose : la découpe ne bouge pas la couverture d'un statement. Ce n'est plus une expérience, c'est le défaut.

**La trouvaille la plus sérieuse depuis le début de ce travail.** `handleKeyMsg` résolvait le curseur sur la liste **non filtrée** alors que le tableau était construit sur la filtrée. Avec un filtre actif les deux index divergent : `ctrl+d`, `p`, `→` et `ctrl+w` agissaient sur ce qui se trouvait à cet index dans l'autre liste. Concrètement, tu filtres sur un projet, tu presses `ctrl+d` sur la seule ligne visible, et c'est un **autre groupe** qui part en suppression. `GetShortcuts` avait le même bug, donc même le `ctrl+w` annoncé se basait sur le mauvais nœud. Les deux passent maintenant par `visibleItems()`, et les fixtures du test sont choisies pour que les deux index ne puissent pas coïncider par accident.

Deux autres corrigées au passage : le curseur bloqué (identique à workspaces, ici seulement sur le chemin filtre — le drill-down était déjà sauvé par son `GotoTop()`), et un message de footer sans timer sur l'échec de suppression (Rule 128) alors que le handler du navigateur, dans le même fichier, le faisait correctement.

**Dérive de l'aide, quatrième vue d'affilée** — `/` annoncé, absent de l'aide. Le check attrapé au premier run. Reste `security` à vérifier.

**Une nouvelle entrée D10** : quand le registre OCI est injoignable, `SetTemplateWarning` est bien appelé, mais `renderTemplateList` retourne tôt quand le champ n'a pas le focus, et l'avertissement est écrit après ce return. L'utilisateur voit une liste de templates vide sans rien qui distingue « le registre a échoué » de « il n'y a pas de template ». Il faut quatre frappes pour l'atteindre. Laissée ouverte : c'est un composant partagé. Le test épingle les deux sens, il échouera aussi quand quelqu'un corrigera.

**La règle que ce paquet a fixée**, et qui explique qu'il monte plus haut que les deux autres malgré une surface I/O bien plus grande : **exécuter la commande dès que la dépendance peut être montée localement**. `httptest` pour l'API GitLab et le registre OCI, un vrai dépôt git semé pour le clone — l'« hôte GitLab » est un répertoire local, donc `recursivePull` clone réellement et écrit réellement l'arborescence. C'est ce qui prouve que la structure de dossiers reflète la hiérarchie de groupes, qu'un checkout existant est ignoré et non écrasé, et qu'un groupe jamais parcouru est chargé en cours de pull. Seul le navigateur reste non exécuté.

Un incident à noter : le premier run CI a échoué là où le local passait. Mon faux serveur routait en itérant une map, et `/api/v4/groups/1/members/all/1` matche deux préfixes — Go randomise l'ordre, donc une fois sur deux le lookup de membre décodait une liste de groupes. Préfixes triés du plus long au plus court, vérifié avec `-count=20`.

Reste en phase 3 : `security` (1977 lignes), le dernier.
continue

With the redirect in place the cache commands are **executed** rather than asserted on identity, in line with what explorer settled.

The most worthwhile tests are not about the state machine. `extractMeaningfulLines` reduces a wall of Trivy and Gitleaks stderr to the one line that explains a failure, so the tests are about what it *discards* — INFO lines, progress bars, the doubled `Fatal error / run error:` wrapping — and about the fallback that shows the raw text rather than an empty panel when nothing matches.

## An assumption corrected

The backlog predicted `security` would carry the same help drift as the four views before it. It does not: its help documents every key its header advertises, across all four states. The three views that carried the drift were the ones where Rule 111 renamed a binding and the help was not updated with it.

content.text:
**Phase 3 terminée.** Dernier paquet, `security` : https://github.com/anthnel/devdesk/pull/18 — CI verte.

| | Couverture | `model.go` |
|---|---|---|
| avant | 0 % | 1991 lignes |
| étape 1 (surface) | **52,9 %** | 1991 |
| étape 2 (découpe) | **52,9 %** | **245** |
| étape 3 (complément) | **83,7 %** | 245 |
| global | 49,3 % → **55,3 %** | |

Le bilan de la phase, quatre paquets : netdiag 86,1 %, workspaces 81,3 %, explorer 91,5 %, security 83,7 %. **La découpe n'a jamais bougé la couverture d'un seul statement**, y compris sur le plus gros fichier du projet. Ce n'est plus un pari, c'est la méthode pour les phases 4 et 5. Il reste trois fichiers au-dessus de 800 lignes, tous en dehors des vues couvertes : `oci_resources/update.go`, `app/app.go`, `oci_resources/registry_browser.go`.

**Deux corrections.** La Rule 128 n'était honorée **nulle part** dans cette vue : `statusMessage` était posé à trois endroits et aucun timer n'existait dans le paquet, donc le dernier message restait affiché jusqu'à ce qu'un changement d'onglet le remette à zéro par hasard. Et `parseVersion` cherchait le premier token commençant par `v` — `gitleaks version 8.18.2` affichait donc « version » comme numéro de version. Son `result[:15]` est devenu `theme.TruncateWidth` : c'est le **sixième et dernier site** de la famille byte-vs-rune que le backlog demandait de traquer. Un grep de `[:` sur des strings dans `internal/ui` ne renvoie plus que de l'indexation de slices.

**Une nouvelle entrée D11** : `getSeverityStyle` construit le style CRITICAL à la main en `ColorError` + `Bold`, ce qui est exactement le `StatusErrorStyle` qu'il renvoie pour HIGH — les deux sont identiques octet pour octet. Dans la vue détail, on ne distingue pas un critique d'un high, alors que la table des findings les distingue correctement via `theme.TableStylesForSeverity`. C'est aussi une violation de la Rule 102. Laissée ouverte : ça change des couleurs que tu lis déjà. Le test est volontairement inversé, il cassera quand quelqu'un branchera la palette.

Deux notes de méthode. `HOME` est redirigé pour tout le paquet — ce n'est pas du confort : chaque case cochée appelle `config.Save`, donc sans ça les tests réécriraient ton `~/.devdesk`. Et les tests qui valent le plus cher ne portent pas sur la machine à états mais sur `extractMeaningfulLines`, qui réduit un mur de stderr Trivy/Gitleaks à la ligne qui explique l'échec : ils portent sur ce qui est **jeté** (lignes INFO, barres de progression, le double emballage `Fatal error / run error:`) et sur le repli qui affiche le texte brut plutôt qu'un panneau vide.

Enfin, une hypothèse du backlog corrigée : je prédisais que `security` aurait la même dérive d'aide que les quatre vues précédentes. Non — son aide documente chaque touche annoncée, dans les quatre états. Les trois vues touchées étaient celles où la Rule 111 avait renommé un binding sans que l'aide suive.

**Cinq défauts attendent ta décision** : D4 (Tab→↑/↓ dans la modale de suppression), D8 (flags CRUD morts), D9 (`sortAsc: true` dans containers), D10 (avertissement registre invisible), D11 (couleurs de sévérité). Chacun fait une à trois lignes ; leur seul coût est de changer ce que l'utilisateur voit déjà.

Ensuite : phase 4, `ui/oci_resources` (~1 995 statements, et deux des trois fichiers restants au-dessus du plafond).
traitons les défauts
Les cinq ont une réponse claire dans les règles du projet ; ce qui les bloquait, c'est qu'ils changent ce que tu vois. Tu tranches, donc je les fais tous — une branche, un commit par défaut.

and read in none: the view keys off componentForm != nil and confirmModal != nil
instead. HasActiveForm, the one method that read them, had been commented out.

stores that — so its case in Update() could not run, and that case was the only
thing that reset creating/editing. State that lies is worse than no state: a
reader reasonably assumes those fields mean something.

Deleting is the smaller of the two fixes and matches how the view already
works. Nothing else changes: the tests already asserted on componentForm and
confirmModal rather than on the flags, which is what made this safe.

### 1.2 The five parked defects

D4, D8, D9, D10 and D11 were each recorded rather than fixed on discovery,
because each changed something the user already saw. They were decided together
and fixed in one pass. Three of the five had a test written to fail *on the
fix*, and all three did.

**D4 — `tab` navigated the delete confirmation.** Rule 135 reserves `tab` for
switching tabs and assigns field navigation to `↑ / ↓` exclusively; the modal
had it exactly inverted, cycling on `tab` and clamping on `↑ / ↓`. `↑ / ↓` now
cycle, which is what keeps every control reachable in one direction, and the
`tab` cases are gone. The explorer no longer advertises "tab Navigate" while the
modal is open, and `↑↓` is not advertised in its place — Rule 138 calls it
obvious. The permanent variant still skips its locked checkbox, so cycling there
toggles between the two buttons.

**D8 — write-only CRUD flags.** `creating`, `editing` and `confirming` were
assigned in five places and read in none, and `ComponentFormCancelledMsg` — the
only thing that would have reset two of them — could never be sent. Deleted, all
of it. Nothing else changed: the phase 2 tests had deliberately asserted on
`componentForm` / `confirmModal` rather than on the flags, which is what made
this safe a phase later.

**D9 — the containers list opened Z→A.** `New()` set neither `sortColumn` nor
`sortAsc`, so both took their zero value. Both are now set explicitly, so the
default is stated rather than inherited. `TestDefaultSortIsNameDescending`
became `TestDefaultSortIsNameAscending`, and the cycle test walks forward from
ascending. The `loadedModel` helper still sets the sort itself even though it
now matches the constructor: those tests should say which order they rely on.

**D10 — a registry failure was invisible.** `renderTemplateList` returned early
when the field was unfocused and the warning sat below that return, so a form
opened after the OCI registry failed offered a Template field reading "none"
with nothing to distinguish "the registry is down" from "there are no
templates". The warning moved into `renderTemplateWarning` and is appended in
both branches — it explains why the list is empty, so it belongs wherever the
list is.

**D11 — CRITICAL and HIGH rendered identically.** `getSeverityStyle` composed
CRITICAL by hand as `ColorError` + `Bold`, which is byte-for-byte the
`theme.StatusErrorStyle` it returned for HIGH. The palette moved to
`theme.SeverityTextStyle`, next to the `TableStylesForSeverity` it draws from,
and the view delegates (Rule 102). An unrecognised severity now falls back to
the info colour rather than to `DimStyle`, so it is still legible.

The pattern worth keeping: when a defect is recorded rather than fixed, write
the test **inverted** — asserting the current behaviour and saying so. D9, D10
and D11 each had one, and each failed the moment the fix landed, which is how
the stale test and the stale backlog entry got found together.

content.text:
Les cinq sont corrigés : https://github.com/anthnel/devdesk/pull/19 — CI verte, un commit par défaut. **§1 du backlog n'a plus rien d'ouvert.**

| | Ce que c'était | Ce qui change |
|---|---|---|
| **D4** | `tab` naviguait dans la modale, `↑ / ↓` clampaient — Rule 135 à l'envers | `↑ / ↓` cyclent, les cas `tab` disparaissent |
| **D8** | trois flags assignés à cinq endroits, lus nulle part | supprimés, avec le message qui ne pouvait jamais partir |
| **D9** | la liste containers ouvrait en Z→A depuis une valeur zéro | `sortColumn` et `sortAsc` posés explicitement |
| **D10** | l'échec du registre invisible tant que Template n'avait pas le focus | l'avertissement s'affiche dans les deux branches |
| **D11** | CRITICAL et HIGH identiques dans le détail | la palette part dans `theme.SeverityTextStyle` |

Quelques choix qui méritent un mot. Pour **D4**, `↑ / ↓` *cyclent* maintenant au lieu de clamper — c'est ce qui garde chaque contrôle atteignable dans un seul sens, exactement ce que `tab` fournissait. Je n'ai pas mis `↑↓` dans les raccourcis annoncés à la place : la Rule 138 le classe comme évident.

Pour **D8**, `ComponentFormCancelledMsg` est parti aussi. Il n'était jamais envoyé — `ComponentForm.handleKeyMsg` répond à `esc` en renvoyant un formulaire nil et l'appelant stocke ça — donc son `case` ne pouvait pas s'exécuter, et ce `case` était la seule chose qui remettait `creating`/`editing` à zéro. La suppression a été sûre parce que les tests de la phase 2 assertaient délibérément sur `componentForm` / `confirmModal` plutôt que sur les flags : une décision prise une phase plus tôt qui paye ici.

Pour **D11**, la palette est allée dans le thème à côté du `TableStylesForSeverity` dont elle dérive, plutôt que d'être recomposée sur place (Rule 102). Toute vue qui doit afficher une sévérité en texte l'a maintenant. Une sévérité inconnue tombe sur la couleur info au lieu de `DimStyle`, donc elle reste lisible.

**Le point de méthode qui vaut d'être gardé** : D9, D10 et D11 avaient chacun un test écrit **à l'envers** — assertant le comportement courant en disant dans son propre commentaire qu'il devait casser à la correction. Les trois ont cassé au premier run. C'est ce qui fait qu'on retrouve le test périmé *et* l'entrée de backlog périmée ensemble, au lieu que l'un survive à l'autre.

Couverture globale 55,3 % → 55,2 % : la suppression D8 a retiré des statements couverts en même temps que le code mort.

Prochaine étape : phase 4, `ui/oci_resources` (~1 995 statements, et deux des trois fichiers encore au-dessus des 800 lignes).

content.text:
Étape 1 de la phase 4 posée. `oci_resources` : 0 % → **25,1 %**.

Ce chiffre est bien en dessous des 52–60 % que les paquets de la phase 3 atteignaient à ce stade, et c'est délibéré : ce paquet fait **6 039 lignes sur onze fichiers**, dont l'essentiel est du code de formulaire et de rendu que la découpe ne touche pas. Ce qui compte pour l'étape 2, c'est le filet sous les deux fichiers au-dessus du plafond — `update.go` est à 60/86 fonctions, `registry_browser.go` à 16/45.

**Trois défauts, chacun épinglé par un test qui a échoué d'abord :**

Quand Docker est éteint, l'onglet Images affiche « Failed to load images — check logs ». Les onglets **Networks et Volumes se contentaient de logger** : table vide, indiscernable de « tu n'as aucun réseau ». Les deux gestionnaires font maintenant ce que leur frère `handleImagesList` fait depuis toujours.

En basculant sur l'onglet **Registries, la table restait vide** jusqu'à ce qu'un contrôle `docker login` asynchrone réponde — alors que les registres viennent du fichier de config et sont disponibles immédiatement. `updateRegistryTable()` s'exécute maintenant au changement d'onglet.

`AddRegistryTags` décrémentait `pendingSearches` **sans plancher**. Une réponse dupliquée ou tardive le rendait négatif, et la recherche suivante repartait de cette base : `IsSearching()` restait faux pendant que des requêtes étaient réellement en vol, donc le spinner ne s'affichait jamais. Plancher à zéro.

Sur la méthode : j'ai écrit une bonne partie de ces tests sur des hypothèses fausses — je supposais que `A` émettait un `ScanAllRequestMsg`, que le prune rapportait un message de succès, que le login remplissait `infoMsg`. Le code fait autre chose dans les trois cas, et souvent mieux (un prune réussi recharge la liste plutôt que d'ajouter du bruit dans le footer). J'ai corrigé les tests vers le comportement réel plutôt que l'inverse.

Reste pour ce paquet : l'étape 2 (découpe de `update.go` 1 698 lignes et `registry_browser.go` 912) puis l'étape 3 (complément, où l'essentiel du gain sera dans `view.go`, les quatre formulaires et `commands.go`). Je continue ?

**Two tabs said nothing when Docker was down.** `handleImagesList` has always set a footer message on failure; `handleNetworksList` and `handleVolumesList` only logged. With the daemon stopped, those two tabs showed an empty table — indistinguishable from "you have no networks".

## A note on method

A good share of these tests were written on wrong assumptions — that `A` emitted a `ScanAllRequestMsg`, that a successful prune reported a message, that a login filled `infoMsg`. The code does something different in each case, and usually better: a successful prune refetches rather than adding footer noise. The tests were corrected toward the real behaviour, not the reverse.

- [x] Split verified as a pure move: no line outside an import block differs.

Phase 4 terminée : https://github.com/anthnel/devdesk/pull/20 — CI verte.

| | Couverture | `update.go` | `registry_browser.go` |

| avant | 0 % | 1707 | 918 |

Le plus gros saut de couverture depuis le début. **Il ne reste qu'un fichier au-dessus des 800 lignes** dans tout le projet : `internal/app/app.go`, que la phase 5 couvre.

**Trois défauts corrigés à l'étape 1.** Quand le démon Docker est éteint, `handleImagesList` a toujours affiché un message ; **Networks et Volumes se contentaient de logger** — table vide, indiscernable de « tu n'as aucun réseau ». En basculant sur **Registries, la table restait vide** jusqu'à ce qu'un contrôle `docker login` asynchrone réponde, alors que les registres viennent du fichier de config. Et `AddRegistryTags` décrémentait `pendingSearches` **sans plancher** : une réponse dupliquée le rendait négatif, la recherche suivante repartait de cette base, et son spinner ne s'affichait jamais.

**Dérive de l'aide, cinquième vue et pire instance.** Networks et Volumes documentaient `n` là où le binding est `ctrl+n` depuis la Rule 111 — même dérive que status et workspaces. Mais **tout l'onglet Registries était non documenté** : `ctrl+n`, `e`, `l`, `L` n'apparaissaient nulle part, quatre actions atteignables uniquement en devinant. Le check a demandé un ajustement ici : l'aide de cette vue qualifie les touches par onglet (`enter (Images)`), donc la parenthèse tombe avant comparaison — avec quatre onglets qui partagent un keymap, cette convention mérite d'être gardée.

**Deux enseignements.** D'abord : **juger la passe de surface sur le fichier qu'on va découper, pas sur le total du paquet.** 25,1 % paraissait maigre à côté des 52–60 % de la phase 3, et ça n'a rien changé — `update.go` était à 60/86 fonctions au moment de la coupe, c'est ça qu'une découpe demande. Ensuite : c'est **le seul paquet laissé sous les 80 %, délibérément**. +#### Allow-list construction beats scrubbing
+
+The post scrubs because it hooks arbitrary agent traffic and cannot know what is
+in it. DevDesk is not in that position: it **assembles the payload itself** from
+`m.results`, which is already typed and structured. So the payload should be
+built field by field from an explicit allow-list, not produced as a blob and
+then cleaned.
+
+The difference matters: **a field never included cannot fail to be redacted.**
+Scrubbing is a filter that can miss; construction is a whitelist that cannot.
+Presidio then runs over the assembled payload as a check on the construction,
+and any hit is a bug in the allow-list, not a routine save.
+
+#### The tension: the sensitive data *is* the diagnostic data
+
+Redacting addresses out of a network diagnostic destroys the diagnostic. A model
+told `[IP_REDACTED]` resolves to `[IP_REDACTED]` can conclude nothing, and the
+answer that comes back is unreadable.
+
+The resolution is **consistent pseudonymisation that preserves the analytically
+relevant class**, not blanket redaction:
+
+| Real | Sent | Preserved |
+|---|---|---|
+| `api.corp.internal` | `host-1` | identity across the payload |
+| `10.2.3.4` | `private-a` | RFC1918, and same-subnet relations |
+| `203.0.113.9` | `public-b` | routable, distinct from private |
+| `10.2.3.7` | `private-c` | same /24 as `private-a` |
+
+The hypotheses the model is asked to rank depend on structure — private vs
+public, same subnet or not, resolves or not, port open or filtered, which TLS
+stage failed — never on the literal octets. So this loses nothing. "host-1
+resolves to private-a but hop 5 is public-c, so the route leaves your network"
+is exactly as useful as the version with real addresses.
+
+The mapping stays in memory, and the response is **restored locally before
+display**, so the user reads real names. The blog post does not do this
+round-trip — its tokens are one-way — but DevDesk needs it, because unlike a
+CSV of customers its payload is *entirely* made of identifiers.
+
+#### Confirmation before send
+
+The assembled, pseudonymised payload is rendered in the viewport before it
+leaves, for every provider. Decision 4 says local and remote are treated alike,
+so there is no "trusted endpoint" shortcut. This costs one keypress and is what
+makes the feature auditable without reading the source.
+
+#### Bubble Tea shape
+
+Streaming is the only delicate part. Rule 110 forbids mutating the model inside
+a `Cmd`, so the pattern is a channel plus a `Cmd` that reads one chunk and
+returns a `streamChunkMsg{gen, text}` which re-arms itself — the same shape as
+the spinner, reusing the generation counter already in `run.go:33` to discard a
+superseded stream.
+
+Cancellation is mandatory, not optional: a local model on CPU can take minutes.
+A `context.CancelFunc` lives in the model and `esc` cancels. **D13 is the
+warning** — a state the user cannot leave while something resolves is a defect
+this repository already has once.
+
+No new view and no command. The explanation is a results tab under the table
+(Rule 123), triggered by a key on the results screen. A dedicated view turns
+this into a chat product, which is not what is being asked for. With no provider
+configured the shortcut is absent rather than erroring (Rule 130), and all
+strings are English US (Rule 129).
+
+#### Sketch of the work
+
+1. `internal/ai`: config block, an OpenAI-compatible client behind a small
+   interface so tests inject a fake — the `runner` indirection in
+   `internal/docker` is the precedent — and the token read from the §3.9 store.
+2. The payload builder: allow-listed fields out of `m.results`, plus the
+   pseudonymiser and its inverse. Table-driven tests, like the existing
+   `dns_formatter` and `traceroute_formatter` parsers. **This is the feature; do
+   it first and it is testable with no endpoint at all.**
+3. The prompt: observed facts only, and an instruction to name which test each
+   claim rests on. The raw results stay on screen next to the explanation —
+   the narrative never replaces the data.
+4. Streaming, cancellation, and the results tab.
+5. The confirmation pane.
+6. Optional and last: Presidio as a fail-closed second net over the assembled
+   payload, behind a config flag. Two containers and a spaCy model is heavy
+   for a few kilobytes of already-structured text, and step 2 is what actually
+   provides the guarantee.
+
+Later, and explicitly not now: capture as an additional input (bounded by `-c`
+and `-G`, `-s 96` by default so payloads cannot be captured at all), and the
+deterministic flow summariser that would have to precede it — a pcap does not
+fit in a context window, and once the summariser exists it answers most of the
+question without a model. `nicolaka/netshoot` (`config.go:218`) already ships
+`tcpdump` and `tshark`, and the privileged host-namespace runner exists
+(`ports.go:36`, `topology.go:47`), so the missing piece is the analysis, not the
+plumbing.
+
+Adjacent candidates, ranked, none settled: Trivy remediation (§3.2 — low
+sensitivity, but any suggested base-image bump must be verified by a re-scan,
+never trusted); Gitleaks triage (highest value since false positives dominate,
+highest risk since the payload *is* the secret — possibly viable by sending rule
+name, path and entropy with the match withheld); container log explanation
+(logs carry env vars and DSNs routinely).
+
+---
+

 Detailed plans live in `.claude/plans/`. One is referenced directly from the old

234	// tryAutoLogin tente de se connecter automatiquement à GitLab avec les credentials sauvegardés
235	func (a *App) tryAutoLogin() tea.Cmd {
236		url := a.config.GitLab.URL
237		currentContext := a.currentContext
238	
239		// Si pas d'URL configurée, pas d'auto-login
240		if url == "" {
241			return nil
242		}
243	
244		return func() tea.Msg {
245			storage := credentials.NewChainStorage(
246				credentials.NewFileStorageForContext(currentContext),
247				credentials.NewGitCredentialStorageWithContext(currentContext),
248			)
249			auth := gitlab.NewAuth(storage)
250	
251			// Essayer de charger le token depuis le storage
252			token, err := auth.LoadCredentials(url)
253			if err != nil || token == "" {
254				// Essayer de charger depuis la config en fallback
255				token = a.config.GitLab.Token
256				if token == "" {
257					// Pas de credentials disponibles, pas d'auto-login
258					return GitLabAutoLoginMsg{Client: nil, User: nil, Error: nil}
259				}
260			}
261	
262			// Authentifier avec le token trouvé
263			result, err := auth.Authenticate(url, token, false) // false = ne pas re-sauvegarder
264			if err != nil {
265				log.Printf("Auto-login failed: %v", err)
266				return GitLabAutoLoginMsg{Client: nil, User: nil, Error: err}
267			}
268	
269			log.Printf("Auto-login successful: %s", result.User.Username)
270			return GitLabAutoLoginMsg{
271				Client: result.Client,
272				User:   result.User,
273				Error:  nil,
274			}
275		}
276	}

278	func (a *App) resize(width, height int) {
279		a.width = width
280		a.height = height
281	
282		// Rule 124: footer height is deducted from the viewport (tabs + optional info line)
283		footerHeight := a.getFooterHeight()
284		a.lastFooterHeight = footerHeight
285	
286		headerHeight := lipgloss.Height(a.renderHeader())
287		availableHeight := height - headerHeight - footerHeight
288		a.viewport.Width = width
289		a.viewport.Height = availableHeight - 1 // -1 for the custom title border line
290		a.viewport.Style = lipgloss.NewStyle().
291			Background(theme.ColorBackground).
292			Foreground(theme.ColorText).
293			Border(lipgloss.NormalBorder(), false, true, true, true).
294			BorderForeground(theme.ColorViewportBorder).
295			BorderBackground(theme.ColorBackground)
296	
297		// Propager à la vue active.
298		// Le viewport a 1 bordure (bottom only), la vue doit connaître la hauteur intérieure.
299		viewportBorderHeight := 1
300		contentHeight := (availableHeight - 1) - viewportBorderHeight
301		if contentHeight < 1 {
302			contentHeight = 1
303		}
304		if view, ok := a.views[a.currentView]; ok {
305			adjustedMsg := tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: width, Height: contentHeight}
306			updatedView, _ := view.Update(adjustedMsg)
307			a.views[a.currentView] = updatedView
308		}
309	}

321	// replaceViewportBottomCorners replaces the bottom-left └ and bottom-right ┘ of the
322	// viewport's bottom border with T-junction chars ├ and ┤, so the filter bar (rendered
323	// in the footer) visually connects with the viewport border to form a closed rectangle.
324	func replaceViewportBottomCorners(body string) string {
325		lastNewline := strings.LastIndex(body, "\n")
326		if lastNewline == -1 {
327			return body
328		}
329		lastLine := body[lastNewline+1:]
330		// Replace first └ with ├ and last ┘ with ┤ in the bottom border line.
331		lastLine = strings.Replace(lastLine, "└", "├", 1)
332		lastLine = strings.Replace(lastLine, "┘", "┤", 1)
333		return body[:lastNewline+1] + lastLine
334	}

336	// switchContext handles context switching with auto-creation
337	func (a *App) switchContext(contextName string) tea.Cmd {
338		return func() tea.Msg {
339			log.Printf("Context switch requested: %s", contextName)
340	
341			// Valider le nom du contexte
342			if err := config.ValidateContextName(contextName); err != nil {
343				log.Printf("ERROR: Context validation failed: %v", err)
344				return ContextSwitchErrorMsg{Error: err}
345			}
346	
347			// Vérifier si le contexte existe
348			exists, err := config.ContextExists(contextName)
349			if err != nil {
350				log.Printf("ERROR: Failed to check context existence: %v", err)
351				return ContextSwitchErrorMsg{Error: err}
352			}
353	
354			// Si le contexte n'existe pas, le créer automatiquement
355			created := false
356			if !exists {
357				log.Printf("Context '%s' does not exist, creating automatically", contextName)
358				if err := config.CreateContext(contextName); err != nil {
359					log.Printf("ERROR: Failed to create context '%s': %v", contextName, err)
360					return ContextSwitchErrorMsg{Error: err}
361				}
362				created = true
363				log.Printf("Context '%s' created successfully", contextName)
364			}
365	
366			// Charger la configuration du contexte
367			cfg, err := config.LoadContext(contextName)
368			if err != nil {
369				log.Printf("ERROR: Failed to load context '%s': %v", contextName, err)
370				return ContextSwitchErrorMsg{Error: err}
371			}
372	
373			// Persister le changement de contexte
374			if err := config.SetCurrentContext(contextName); err != nil {
375				log.Printf("ERROR: Failed to persist context switch: %v", err)
376				return ContextSwitchErrorMsg{Error: err}
377			}
378	
379			// Attempt auto-login with the new context's credentials
380			var glClient *gitlabclient.Client
381			var glUser *gitlabclient.User
382			if cfg.GitLab.URL != "" {
383				storage := credentials.NewChainStorage(
384					credentials.NewFileStorageForContext(contextName),
385					credentials.NewGitCredentialStorageWithContext(contextName),
386				)
387				gitlabAuth := gitlab.NewAuth(storage)
388				token, err := gitlabAuth.LoadCredentials(cfg.GitLab.URL)
389				if err != nil || token == "" {
390					token = cfg.GitLab.Token
391				}
392				if token != "" {
393					result, err := gitlabAuth.Authenticate(cfg.GitLab.URL, token, false)
394					if err == nil {
395						glClient = result.Client
396						glUser = result.User
397						log.Printf("Auto-login successful for context '%s': %s", contextName, glUser.Username)
398					} else {
399						log.Printf("Auto-login failed for context '%s': %v", contextName, err)
400					}
401				}
402			}
403	
404			log.Printf("Context switch successful: %s (created: %v)", contextName, created)
405			return ContextSwitchCompleteMsg{
406				ContextName:  contextName,
407				Config:       cfg,
408				Created:      created,
409				GitLabClient: glClient,
410				GitLabUser:   glUser,
411			}
412		}
413	}

438	// handleKeyMsg processes keyboard input
439	func (a *App) handleKeyMsg(msg tea.KeyMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
440		// Si un overlay est affiché, gérer la navigation
441		if a.showHelp {
442			return a.handleHelpKeyMsg(msg)
443		}
444		if a.showContextList {
445			return a.handleContextListKeyMsg(msg)
446		}
447		if a.showThemeList {
448			return a.handleThemeListKeyMsg(msg)
449		}
450	
451		if a.commandMode {
452			return a.handleCommandMode(msg)
453		}
454	
455		switch msg.String() {
456		case "ctrl+c":
457			return a, tea.Quit
458		case "q":
459			cmd := a.maybeQuitApplication(msg)
460			return a, cmd
461		case "?":
462			return a.maybeOpenHelp(msg)
463		case altCommandModeKey:
464			// The authoritative way in: handled here, before any InEditMode() check,
465			// so no text input can claim it. A bare ":" cannot play that role — it is
466			// an ordinary character in a field holding https://trivy-server:4954.
467			return a, a.enterCommandMode()
468		case ":":
469			cmd := a.maybeEnterInCommandMode(msg)
470			return a, cmd
471		case "esc":
472			cmd := a.maybeQuitCommandMode(msg)
473			// Rule 124: re-resize if a form was closed and footer height changed
474			if newFooterHeight := a.getFooterHeight(); newFooterHeight != a.lastFooterHeight {
475				a.resize(a.width, a.height)
476			}
477			return a, cmd
478		default:
479			if view, ok := a.views[a.currentView]; ok {
480				updatedView, cmd := view.Update(msg)
481				a.views[a.currentView] = updatedView
482				// Re-resize if the view's footer height changed (e.g., filter bar toggled).
483				if newFooterHeight := a.getFooterHeight(); newFooterHeight != a.lastFooterHeight {
484					a.resize(a.width, a.height)
485				}
486				return a, cmd
487			}
488			return a, nil
489		}
490	}

494		a.config = msg.Config
495		a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
496	
497		// Reset GitLab auth state — the new context has its own credentials
498		a.sharedState.GitLabClient = nil
499		a.sharedState.IsAuthenticated = false
500		a.sharedState.CurrentUser = nil
501		a.sharedState.CachedGroups = nil
502		a.sharedState.CachedProjects = nil
503		a.sharedState.GitLabStats = nil
504	
505		// Apply auto-login result from the context switch if successful
506		if msg.GitLabClient != nil && msg.GitLabUser != nil {
507			a.sharedState.GitLabClient = msg.GitLabClient
508			a.sharedState.CurrentUser = msg.GitLabUser
509			a.sharedState.IsAuthenticated = true
510		} else {
511			// No credentials available — navigate to auth view for manual login
512			a.currentView = command.ViewGitlabAuth
513		}
514	
515		// Reinitialize views with new config; auth state is already populated above
516		initCmd := a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
517	
518		windowSizeCmd := func() tea.Msg {
519			return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
520		}
521		return a, tea.Batch(windowSizeCmd, initCmd)
522	}

562	
563		// Sauvegarder la configuration sur le disque

571		}
572	
573		// Transmettre le message à la vue pour mise à jour de l'UI
574		if view, ok := a.views[a.currentView]; ok {
575			updatedView, cmd := view.Update(msg)
576			a.views[a.currentView] = updatedView

578		}

1065	func (a *App) Update(msg tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
1066		switch msg := msg.(type) {
1067		case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
1068			a.resize(msg.Width, msg.Height)
1069			return a, nil
1070	
1071		case tea.KeyMsg:
1072			return a.handleKeyMsg(msg)
1073	
1074		case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
1075			return a.handleContextSwitchComplete(msg)
1076	
1077		case ContextSwitchErrorMsg:
1078			log.Printf("ERROR: Context operation failed: %v", msg.Error)
1079			// Future: afficher l'erreur dans status bar
1080			return a, nil
1081	
1082		case ContextListMsg:
1083			// Afficher l'overlay avec la liste des contextes
1084			a.showContextList = true
1085			a.contextList = msg.Contexts
1086			// Positionner la sélection sur le contexte courant
1087			a.contextSelectedIdx = 0
1088			for i, ctx := range msg.Contexts {
1089				if ctx == msg.Current {
1090					a.contextSelectedIdx = i
1091					break
1092				}
1093			}
1094			return a, nil
1095	
1096		case ThemeListMsg:
1097			// Afficher l'overlay avec la liste des thèmes
1098			a.showThemeList = true
1099			a.themeList = msg.Themes
1100			a.currentTheme = msg.Current
1101			// Positionner la sélection sur le thème courant
1102			a.themeSelectedIdx = 0
1103			for i, t := range msg.Themes {
1104				if t == msg.Current {
1105					a.themeSelectedIdx = i
1106					break
1107				}
1108			}
1109			return a, nil
1110	
1111		case ThemeAppliedMsg:
1112			return a.handleThemeApplied(msg)
1113	
1114		case ThemeErrorMsg:
1115			log.Printf("ERROR: Theme operation failed: %v", msg.Error)
1116			return a, nil
1117	
1118		case auth.AuthResultMsg:
1119			// Intercepter l'authentification GitLab pour sauvegarder la config et mettre à jour le shared.State
1120			return a.handleAuthResult(msg)
1121	
1122		case GitLabAutoLoginMsg:
1123			return a.handleAutoLoginResult(msg)
1124	
1125		case workspaces.WorkspaceScanCompleteMsg:
1126			// Update workspace view with scan results.
1127			// Don't auto-switch if the user is in the security view: switching would cause the
1128			// security scan's ScanCompleteMsg to be routed to the wrong view, leaving the spinner
1129			// stuck forever (race condition between background batch scan and manual security scan).
1130			if view, ok := a.views[command.ViewWorkspaces]; ok {
1131				updatedView, cmd := view.Update(msg)
1132				a.views[command.ViewWorkspaces] = updatedView
1133				if a.currentView != command.ViewSecurity {
1134					a.currentView = command.ViewWorkspaces
1135				}
1136				return a, cmd
1137			}
1138			return a, nil
1139	
1140		case workspaces.ScanDetailsRequestMsg:
1141			// Workspaces view requests full scan details for a repo
1142			return a.handleWorkspaceScanDetails(msg)
1143	
1144		case WorkspaceScanResultLoadedMsg:
1145			// Cached scan result loaded: open security view in details mode
1146			return a.handleWorkspaceScanResultLoaded(msg)
1147	
1148		case ociresources.ImageScanStartingMsg:
1149			// Route scan progress to OCI images view regardless of current view
1150			return a.routeToOCIImagesView(msg)
1151	
1152		case ociresources.ImageScanFinishedMsg:
1153			// Route scan result to OCI images view regardless of current view
1154			return a.routeToOCIImagesView(msg)
1155	
1156		case ociresources.LaunchBatchScanMsg:
1157			// Security view delegated batch scan back to OCI images view
1158			return a.handleLaunchBatchScan(msg)
1159	
1160		case ociresources.LaunchSingleImageScanMsg:
1161			// Security view delegated single image scan back to OCI images view
1162			return a.handleLaunchSingleImageScan(msg)
1163	
1164		case ociresources.ScanDetailsRequestMsg:
1165			// OCI images view requests scan details for a specific image (loads from cache, no re-scan)
1166			return a.handleScanDetailsRequest(msg)
1167	
1168		case ImageScanResultLoadedMsg:
1169			// Cached image scan result loaded: open security view in details mode
1170			return a.handleImageScanResultLoaded(msg)
1171	
1172		case security.SelectionRequestMsg:
1173			// Security view requests to browse directories or images
1174			return a.handleSelectionRequest(msg)
1175	
1176		case security.BackToOriginMsg:
1177			// User pressed Esc in security results view: return to the originating view
1178			return a, a.switchView(msg.Origin)
1179	
1180		case explorer.PullSelectionRequestMsg:
1181			// Explorer requests workspace selection for pull destination
1182			return a.handleExplorerPullRequest()
1183	
1184		case workspaces.DirectorySelectedMsg:
1185			// Workspaces view returned a selected directory
1186			return a.handleDirectorySelected(msg)
1187	
1188		case workspaces.SelectionCancelledMsg:
1189			// Workspaces view cancelled selection
1190			return a.handleSelectionCancelled()
1191	
1192		case ociresources.ImageSelectedMsg:
1193			// OCI images view returned a selected image
1194			return a.handleImageSelected(msg)
1195	
1196		case ociresources.SelectionCancelledMsg:
1197			// OCI images view cancelled selection
1198			return a.handleSelectionCancelled()
1199	
1200		default:
1201			// Transmettre aux vues
1202			if view, ok := a.views[a.currentView]; ok {
1203				updatedView, cmd := view.Update(msg)
1204				a.views[a.currentView] = updatedView
1205				// Rule 124: re-resize if the view's footer height changed (e.g., security state transitions)
1206				if newFooterHeight := a.getFooterHeight(); newFooterHeight != a.lastFooterHeight {
1207					a.resize(a.width, a.height)
1208				}
1209				return a, cmd
1210			}
1211		}
1212		return a, nil
1213	}

1215	// View rend l'interface
1216	func (a *App) View() string {
1217		// Import lipgloss si nécessaire
1218		var content string
1219	
1220		// Afficher la vue courante
1221		if view, ok := a.views[a.currentView]; ok {
1222			content = view.View()
1223		} else {
1224			content = "View not found: " + string(a.currentView)
1225		}
1226	
1227		// Remplir le contenu sur toute la largeur intérieure du viewport
1228		innerWidth := a.viewport.Width - 2 // -2 pour les bordures
1229		content = lipgloss.NewStyle().
1230			Background(theme.ColorBackground).
1231			Foreground(theme.ColorText).
1232			Width(innerWidth).
1233			Render(content)
1234		a.viewport.SetContent(content)
1235	
1236		header := a.renderHeader()
1237	
1238		// Construire la ligne de bordure supérieure avec le titre de la vue
1239		titleLine := theme.RenderBorderTitle("", a.width)
1240		if view, ok := a.views[a.currentView]; ok {
1241			if hv, implements := view.(HeaderView); implements {
1242				titleLine = theme.RenderBorderTitle(hv.GetTitle(), a.width)
1243			}
1244		}
1245	
1246		body := a.viewport.View()
1247	
1248		// Rule 136: replace viewport bottom corners with T-junctions when filter bar is visible,
1249		// so the viewport bottom border and the filter bar form a fully closed rectangle.
1250		if view, ok := a.views[a.currentView]; ok {
1251			if fbv, ok := view.(FilterBarView); ok && fbv.FilterBarVisible() {
1252				body = replaceViewportBottomCorners(body)
1253			}
1254		}
1255	
1256		// Rule 124: render footer below the viewport bottom border
1257		footer := ""
1258		if view, ok := a.views[a.currentView]; ok {
1259			if fv, ok := view.(FooterView); ok {
1260				footer = fv.RenderFooter(a.width)
1261			}
1262		}
1263	
1264		inner := header + "\n" + titleLine + "\n" + body
1265		if footer != "" {
1266			inner += "\n" + footer
1267		}
1268		mainView := lipgloss.Place(a.width, a.height, lipgloss.Left, lipgloss.Top, inner,
1269			lipgloss.WithWhitespaceBackground(theme.ColorBackground))
1270	
1271		// Si l'overlay d'aide est affiché, le superposer
1272		if a.showHelp {
1273			overlay := a.renderHelpOverlay()
1274			return lipgloss.Place(a.width, a.height, lipgloss.Center, lipgloss.Center, overlay,
1275				lipgloss.WithWhitespaceBackground(theme.ColorBackground))
1276		}
1277	
1278		// Si l'overlay de contextes est affiché, le superposer
1279		if a.showContextList {
1280			overlay := a.renderContextListOverlay()
1281			return lipgloss.Place(a.width, a.height, lipgloss.Center, lipgloss.Center, overlay,
1282				lipgloss.WithWhitespaceBackground(theme.ColorBackground))
1283		}
1284	
1285		// Si l'overlay de thèmes est affiché, le superposer
1286		if a.showThemeList {
1287			overlay := a.renderThemeListOverlay()
1288			return lipgloss.Place(a.width, a.height, lipgloss.Center, lipgloss.Center, overlay,
1289				lipgloss.WithWhitespaceBackground(theme.ColorBackground))
1290		}
1291	
1292		return mainView
1293	}

1354	// handleCommandMode gère le mode commande

1358			// Annuler le mode commande
1359			a.commandMode = false

### 1.3 Open

All three sit in `internal/ui/oci_resources` and are cheap on their own, but
§3.8 rewrites the code path each of them lives in. Fix them **as part of** that
work rather than ahead of it, and write each one's test inverted first, per the
pattern above.

**D12 — `AuthEnabled` has no effect on browse or discovery.** The flag is
honoured in exactly three places: the `docker login` fired on form submit, the
`Logged` column, and the URL list `registryLoginStatusCmd` checks. Neither code
path that actually talks to a registry consults it. `submitSearch`
(`browser_keys.go:142`) calls `docker.GetStoredCreds(credURL)`
unconditionally and hands the result to `searchRegistryTagsCmd`;
`detectRegistryGroupCmd` (`commands.go:563`) does the same before calling into
`registrymgr`. A registry the user has marked as needing no authentication will
still have the host's stored credentials sent to it whenever any other registry
on that host has been logged into — which, given that Docker keys credentials by
host, is the normal case for a Nexus instance. This is the defect the
`anonymous` mode in §3.8 exists to make expressible; today there is no way to
say "do not send credentials here" at all.

**D13 — the browser cannot be dismissed while it is resolving.**
`handleKeyMsg` returns `nil` for every key in `browserStateResolving`
(`browser_keys.go:70`), `esc` included, and that state is entered
unconditionally on open whenever any registry is configured. The detections run
concurrently with an 8 s timeout each, so the wedge is bounded at roughly eight
seconds — but it is eight seconds during which the application ignores the user,
on a screen they may have opened by mistake. §3.8 removes the state rather than
the symptom: with members read from config and cache, there is nothing to
resolve and the form renders immediately.

A smaller thing in the same handler, not worth its own entry:
`HandleGroupDetected` matches the incoming result against `reg.URL`, so two
registries configured with the same URL collide and the second result overwrites
the first. The slug introduced in §3.8 is the natural key to match on instead.

**D14 — the registry filter shows a raw URL for group members.**
`registryFilterLabel()` (`browser_tags.go:63`) resolves the active filter by
searching `b.registries`, which holds only the configured top-level entries.
Discovered members are not in that list, so filtering to one falls through to
returning `b.registryFilter` — the full synthesised URL — where every other row
in the same view shows a short alias. The fix follows from §3.8 rather than
preceding it: once members are persisted they are resolvable, and the filter
gains a group level at the same time.

input.new_string:
preceding it: once members are persisted they are resolvable, and the filter
gains a group level at the same time.

**D15 — `esc` never reaches a view that is not editing.** `handleKeyMsg`
(`keys.go`) answers `esc` itself through `maybeQuitCommandMode`, which forwards
the key only when the view reports `InEditMode()`. Every other time the router
consumes it and returns a resize. The explorer's `esc` → `handleDrillUp`
(`update.go:157`) is therefore dead code: only `←` and `h` drill up, though
Rule 111 lists `esc` as the third way. The explorer's own unit tests pass
because they drive the model directly, bypassing the router — this is precisely
the class of defect router tests exist to catch.

The security view already works around it: `InEditMode()` there is documented as
*"returns true when the view needs to handle ESC key"*, which overloads a
predicate about focused fields into a predicate about key ownership. The fix is
to give `esc` the same shape as every other key — forward it to the view first
and let the router act only if the view did not — but that changes behaviour in
every view at once, so it wants its own commit and a pass over each view's esc
handling. Inverted test:
`TestEscIsSwallowedForAViewThatIsNotEditing` (`router_test.go`).

**D16 — `:netdiag` is documented but not accepted.** `CLAUDE.md` lists
"`netdiag` or `net`", the view is named `netdiag` throughout, and the directory
is `internal/ui/netdiag` — but `viewMap` in `parser.go` has only `"net"`.
`:netdiag` parses to `CommandUnknown`, which leaves the command line open with
no diagnostic. One map entry. Covered by the comment on the `net` row in
`TestEveryNamedViewCanBeReached` (`command_line_test.go`).

**D17 — the completion catalogue is a subset of the parser.**
`buildCommands()` (`completion.go`) lists eight full commands; the parser
accepts fourteen views plus aliases. `gitlab-explorer`, `workspaces`,
`security` and `net` all work when typed in full but cannot be tab-completed,
and nothing keeps the two lists in step. The parser's `viewMap` is the natural
single source — the catalogue should be derived from it rather than restated.
Worth doing with D16, which is the same drift.

**D18 — the header overflows a narrow window.** `buildShortcutLines`
(`app_header.go:202`) intends to clip the shortcut block to its column —
`// Truncate if wider than col2Width` — but calls `theme.PadWithBg`, which
returns the content untouched when it is already at or past the target. Below
roughly 100 columns the header therefore renders wider than the window and
wraps: at width 80 with twelve shortcuts every header row comes out 95 wide.
The fix is `lipgloss.NewStyle().MaxWidth(col2Width)`, which truncates without
cutting an escape sequence in half — the hazard Rule 122 is about. Inverted
test: `TestANarrowHeaderOverflowsTheWindow` (`header_test.go`).

**D19 — the Trivy command shown is not the one run.** `GetTrivyCommand` exists
to display what will be executed, and rebuilds the argument list by hand from
the same inputs as `RunTrivy`. The two have drifted: `RunTrivy` takes
`ignoreEOL` and appends `--ignore-status end_of_life`; `GetTrivyCommand` does
not take the parameter at all. A user copying the logged command gets different
results from the scan they just watched. `RunTrivyMisconfig` and `GenerateSBOM`
have no display counterpart at all, so their commands are never shown.

The fix is not to add the missing flag but to remove the duplication: extract
one pure `trivyArgs(...)` builder returning the binary name and its arguments,
and have `RunTrivy` turn it into an `exec.Cmd` while `GetTrivyCommand` joins it
into a string. Same for gitleaks. This is planned as the split step of phase 5
for `internal/scan`, since it is also what makes the argument surface testable.

---
